He played [[college basketball]] for the [[USC Trojans men's basketball|USC Trojans]]. ==Early life== Porter was born in [[Seattle|Seattle, Washington]], to Ayanna and Bryan Kevin Porter Sr.{{cite web |title=Kevin Porter Jr. |url=https://usctrojans.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=8800 |publisher=University of Southern California Athletics |access-date=December 28, 2018 |archive-date=January 26, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190126172250/https://usctrojans.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=8800 |url-status=live }} Porter Sr. died in a shooting in 2004 when Porter Jr. was four years old.{{cite web | url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nba/2022/01/06/wizards-announcer-makes-grim-reference-kevin-porter-jr-dead-father/9114176002/ | title=Wizards announcer apologizes to Kevin Porter Jr. For mistaken allusion to player's dead father | website=[[USA Today]] | access-date=March 3, 2022 | archive-date=March 3, 2022 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220303144438/https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nba/2022/01/06/wizards-announcer-makes-grim-reference-kevin-porter-jr-dead-father/9114176002/ | url-status=live }}{{cite web | url=https://sports.yahoo.com/wizards-broadcaster-shocking-trigger-comment-about-kevin-porter-jr-father-rockets-154626390.html | title=Wizards broadcaster makes shocking 'trigger' comment about Kevin Porter Jr.'s father, but was it a mix-up? | date=January 6, 2022 | access-date=March 3, 2022 | archive-date=March 3, 2022 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220303144437/https://sports.yahoo.com/wizards-broadcaster-shocking-trigger-comment-about-kevin-porter-jr-father-rockets-154626390.html | url-status=live }} As a result, Porter Jr. was raised in [[Southend Seattle|South Seattle]] by his mother, who became his role model.{{cite web |last1=Blockus |first1=Gary R. |title=Previously Unheralded Kevin Porter Jr. Looks To Show He Belongs With USA Basketball |url=https://www.usab.com/news-events/news/2018/06/mu18-porter-feature.aspx |publisher=[[USA Basketball]] |access-date=December 28, 2018 |date=June 2, 2018 |archive-date=December 28, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181228223329/https://www.usab.com/news-events/news/2018/06/mu18-porter-feature.aspx |url-status=dead }}{{cite web |last1=Cotterill |first1=TJ |title=Hothead? Bad attitude? No more. Kevin Porter Jr. found a father figure in Jamal Crawford to become state's best player |url=https://www.thenewstribune.com/sports/high-school/article205780354.html |website=[[The News Tribune]] |access-date=December 28, 2018 |date=March 19, 2018 |archive-date=November 20, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181120180243/https://www.thenewstribune.com/sports/high-school/article205780354.html |url-status=live }} ==High school career== Porter convinced his mother to enroll him at Rainier Beach High School instead of [[O'Dea High School]] in Seattle, because his father had played sports there and he wanted to preserve the tradition. In his senior campaign, he averaged 27 points, 14 rebounds, and five assists, as Rainier Beach finished with a 22–7 record. On March 3, 2018, Porter recorded 22 points and 11 rebounds in a Class 3A state championship game loss to [[Garfield High School (Seattle)|Garfield High School]].{{cite web |last1=Evans |first1=Jayda Porter announced his intention to forgo his remaining collegiate eligibility and declare for the [[2019 NBA draft]]. ==Professional career== ===Cleveland Cavaliers (2019–2021)=== [[File:Kevin porter [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] via the [[Detroit Pistons]].{{cite web|title=Detroit Pistons Acquire Tony Snell and Draft Rights to 30th Pick Kevin Porter that they had signed Porter.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/draft-picks-signings-190703|title=Cavaliers Sign Garland, Windler and Porter Jr.|date=July 3, playing in an 85–94 loss to the [[Orlando Magic]] and finishing with one rebound, two assists, and a steal.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401160627|title=Magic, Vucevic beat Cavaliers in season opener|date=October 23, 2019|website=ESPN.com|access-date=October 23, 2019|archive-date=September 19, web|url=https://www.cleveland.com/cavs/2019/11/kevin-porter-jrs-dope-first-nba-start-shows-how-far-hes-come-in-short-time-fedors-five-observations.html|title=Kevin Porter Jr's 'dope' first NBA start Porter started the 2020–21 season inactive due to his off-season weapons charge, which was later dropped.{{cite January 18, 2021, the Cavaliers announced that Porter would either be traded or released following an outburst regarding a locker change following the Cavaliers' acquisition of [[Taurean Prince]] from the [[Brooklyn Nets]]. He was traded to the Rockets three days later, having not played a single game with the Cavaliers in the 2020–21 season.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/30756372/source-cleveland-cavaliers-trading-kevin-porter-jr-houston-rockets-second-round-pick|title=Cleveland Cavaliers trade Kevin Porter Jr. to Houston Rockets|website=ESPN.com|last1=MacMahon|first1=Tim|last2=Wojnarowski|first2=Adrian|date=January 22, 2021|access-date=November 29, 2021|archive-date=November 30, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211130055628/https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/30756372/source-cleveland-cavaliers-trading-kevin-porter-jr-houston-rockets-second-round-pick|url-status=live}} ===Houston Rockets (2021–2023)=== On January 21, 2021, Porter was traded to the [[Houston Rockets]] for a future top-55 protected second round pick.{{cite web|title=Cavaliers Trade Kevin Porter Jr. to Houston|url=https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/porter-jr-trade-210122|website=NBA.com|date=January 22, 2021|access-date=January 21, 2021|archive-date=April 1, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210401073746/https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/porter-jr-trade-210122|url-status=live}}{{cite tweet|number=1352463148310290432|user=espn_macmahon|title=This is a top-55 protected pick that is likely never to convey, per sources. The Rockets are taking a flyer on a ta... |accessdate=2021-07-26|language=en|date=January 22, 2021}} He was later assigned to the Rockets' G League affiliate, the [[Rio Grande Valley Vipers]], debuting for the Vipers in their season opener on February 10, 2021. On February 25, he recorded the first triple-double of the G League season, scoring 27 points, collecting 11 rebounds and dishing out 14 assists.{{cite news|url=https://gleague.nba.com/games/20210225/ERIRGV/|title=Porter Jr. Records First Triple-double Of G League Season In Vipers Big Win Over Bayhawks|publisher=[[NBA G League]]|date=February 25, 2021|access-date=February 26, 2021|archive-date=August 26, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220826094239/https://gleague.nba.com/games/20210225/ERIRGV/|url-status=live}} On March 6, the Rockets officially recalled Porter from the Vipers after an impressive performance in the G-League.{{Cite web |last=Taylor |first=Cody |date=March 6, 2021 |title=Rockets recall Porter, Martin from NBA G League assignment |url=https://therookiewire.usatoday.com/2021/03/06/rockets-recall-kevin-porter-jr-kj-martin-nba-g-league-assignment/ |access-date=January 15, 2023 |archive-date=January 15, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230115072112/https://therookiewire.usatoday.com/2021/03/06/rockets-recall-kevin-porter-jr-kj-martin-nba-g-league-assignment/ |url-status=live }} Porter made his official debut with the Rockets on March 11, 2021, contributing 13 points, ten assists and five rebounds in a game lost against the [[Sacramento Kings]].{{Cite web |last=DuBose |first=Ben |date=March 12, 2021 |title=Kevin Porter Jr. has 'big brother' in former Rockets star James Harden |url=https://rocketswire.usatoday.com/2021/03/12/kevin-porter-jr-has-big-brother-in-former-rockets-star-james-harden/ |access-date=March 12, 2021 |archive-date=March 12, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210312063412/https://rocketswire.usatoday.com/2021/03/12/kevin-porter-jr-has-big-brother-in-former-rockets-star-james-harden/ |url-status=live }} On April 28, Porter was fined $50,000 for violating the league's Health and Safety Protocols.{{Cite web |last=Nba.com |date=April 28, 2021 |title=Rockets guard Kevin Porter Jr. fined $50K |website=[[NBA.com]] |url=https://www.nba.com/news/rockets-guard-kevin-porter-jr-fined-50k |access-date=April 28, 2021 |archive-date=April 28, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210428212255/https://www.nba.com/news/rockets-guard-kevin-porter-jr-fined-50k |url-status=live }} In the next following day after the incident, he scored 50 points and recorded 11 assists in a win against the [[Milwaukee Bucks]], becoming the youngest player in NBA history to have 50+ points and 10+ assists in a game.{{cite tweet|number=1387964843098087428|user=ESPNNBA|title=20-year-old Kevin Porter Jr. is the youngest player in NBA history with 50 points and 10 assists in a game 🚀 🚀 🚀 L... |date=April 30, 2021}} By the end of the regular season, Porter had only played 26 games with the Rockets due to the many conflicts he was dealing with, averaging 16.6 points, 6.3 assists, 3.8 rebounds, and 3.1 turnovers per game. On January 1, 2022, during a 111–124 loss to the Denver Nuggets, Porter and teammate [[Christian Wood]] got into a verbal altercation with Rockets assistant coach [[John Lucas II|John Lucas]] at halftime. Porter then threw an object into the locker room and left the [[Toyota Center]], the arena where the Rockets were playing, before the game ended.{{Cite web|title=Rockets guard Kevin Porter Jr. leaves arena at halftime after heated exchange with assistant coach|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/houston-rockets-kevin-porter-christian-wood-heated-exchange-left-arena-assistant-coach-denver-nuggets-loss-054206083.html|access-date=January 4, 2022|website=Yahoo Sports|date=January 2, 2022 |archive-date=January 5, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220105004509/https://sports.yahoo.com/houston-rockets-kevin-porter-christian-wood-heated-exchange-left-arena-assistant-coach-denver-nuggets-loss-054206083.html|url-status=live}} On January 3, Rockets head coach [[Stephen Silas]] stated that he had suspended both Porter and Wood for one game each for their behavior.{{Cite web|title=Houston Rockets suspend Kevin Porter, Christian Wood one game for poor behavior|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/32986193/houston-rockets-suspend-kevin-porter-christian-wood-poor-behavior-sources-say|access-date=January 4, 2022|website=ESPN|date=January 3, 2022|archive-date=July 17, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220717191150/https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/32986193/houston-rockets-suspend-kevin-porter-christian-wood-poor-behavior-sources-say|url-status=live}} On March 31, 2022, he recorded his first triple double with 30 points, 12 rebounds and 12 assists in a 121–118 loss against Sacramento. On October 17, 2022, Porter agreed on a four-year, $82.5 million contract extension with the Rockets.{{Cite web |title=Kevin Porter Jr. Signs Contract Extension |url=https://www.si.com/nba/rockets/news/houston-rockets-kevin-porter-jr-signs-contract-extension |access-date=October 17, 2022 |website=si.com |date=October 17, 2022 |archive-date=October 17, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221017144610/https://www.si.com/nba/rockets/news/houston-rockets-kevin-porter-jr-signs-contract-extension |url-status=live }} On March 23, 2023, he recorded his second triple double with 14 points, 10 rebounds, and 10 assists in a 130–125 loss against Memphis. On October 17, 2023, Porter was traded to the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] following his domestic assault charge.{{cite web|title=Rockets Complete Trade With Oklahoma City|url=https://www.nba.com/rockets/news/rockets-complete-trade-with-oklahoma-city-2|website=NBA.com|date=October 17, 2023|access-date=October 17, 2023}} However, he was waived after the trade was completed.{{cite tweet|first=Clemente|last=Almanza|title=Thunder PR: Additionally, Oklahoma City acquired the contract of G Kevin Porter Jr. He will be waived immediately.|number=1714434048020377851|user=CAlmanza1007|date=October 17, 2023|access-date=October 17, 2023}} ===PAOK (2024)=== On April 2, 2024, Porter signed with Greek club [[PAOK BC|PAOK]] for the rest of the season.{{cite web|title=O Kevin Porter Jr. έρχεται στη Θεσσαλονίκη για τον ΠΑΟΚ mateco|url=https://www.paokbc.gr/el/nea/omadas/2643-o-kevin-porter-jr-mateco-2|website=PAOKBC.gr|date=April 2, 2024|access-date=April 2, 2024|language=Greek}} In 6 domestic league matches, he averaged 22 points, 9.8 rebounds, 6.8 assists and 2.8 steals in 39 minutes per contest. Porter posted a triple-double against [[Panathinaikos B.C.|Panathinaikos]] with a stat line of 23 points, 14 rebounds and 10 assists, the first in [[Greek Basket League]] playoff history. ===Los Angeles Clippers (2024–2025)=== On July 10, 2024, Porter signed with the [[Los Angeles Clippers]].{{cite web|title=LA Clippers Sign Kevin Porter Jr.|url=https://www.nba.com/clippers/news/la-clippers-sign-kevin-porter-jr|website=NBA.com|date=July 10, 2024|access-date=July 10, 2024}} ===Milwaukee Bucks (2025–present)=== On February 6, 2025, Porter was traded to the [[2024–25 Milwaukee Bucks season|Milwaukee Bucks]] in exchange for [[MarJon Beauchamp]].{{cite web|title=Milwaukee Bucks Acquire Kevin Porter Jr.|url=https://www.nba.com/bucks/news/milwaukee-bucks-acquire-kevin-porter-jr|website=NBA.com|date=February 6, 2025|access-date=February 6, 2025}} On March 5, Porter recorded a 14 assist, 11 rebound, 10 point [[triple-double]] during a 137–110 win over the [[Dallas Mavericks]].{{cite web |title=Bucks' Kevin Porter: Posts rare triple-double in victory |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/bucks-kevin-porter-posts-rare-triple-double-in-victory/ |website=CBSSports.com |publisher=CBS |language=en |date=6 March 2025}} On April 27, during the [[2025 NBA playoffs#(4) Indiana Pacers vs. (5) Milwaukee Bucks|first round]] of the [[2025 NBA playoffs|playoffs]], Porter recorded 23 points, five rebounds, six assists and two steals in a 129–103 Game 4 loss to the [[2024–25 Indiana Pacers season|Indiana Pacers]].{{Cite web |title=Pacers roll to 129-103 victory in Game 4 to take 3-1 lead after Bucks lose Lillard to injury |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401768049 |access-date=April 28, 2025 |website=ESPN}} On June 30, 2025, Porter Jr. agreed to a two-year, $11 million contract to return to the Bucks. The signing was formally completed on July 6, after the [[NBA_salary_cap#July_moratorium|July moratorium]] at the start of the 2025–26 NBA year.{{cite web|url=https://www.si.com/nba/bucks/news/bucks-sign-breakout-guard-to-11-million-deal-in-major-free-agent-move-01jz1hv5smqa|title=Bucks sign breakout guard Kevin Porter Jr. to two-year, $11M deal|publisher=Sports Illustrated|date=June 30, 2025}} On October 31, it was announced that Porter would miss at least four weeks due to a [[meniscus tear|torn meniscus]] in his right knee.{{Cite web|title=Bucks' Kevin Porter Jr. to miss 4 weeks with knee injury|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/46797492/bucks-kevin-porter-jr-miss-4-weeks-right-meniscus-injury|access-date=November 22, 2025|website=espn.com|language=en}} He made 38 appearances (including 36 starts) for Milwaukee during the [[2025–26 NBA season|2025–26 season]], averaging 17.4 points, 5.2 rebounds, and 7.4 assists. On April 7, 2026, Porter underwent [[arthroscopy|arthroscopic]] surgery to repair his right knee and would miss the rest of the team's regular season.{{cite web |title=Kevin Porter Jr. underwent season-ending knee surgery for Bucks |url=https://basketnews.com/news-244620-kevin-porter-jr-underwent-season-ending-knee-surgery-for-bucks.html |website=basketnews.com |access-date=15 April 2026 |language=en}} ==Player profile== [[File:Kevin_Porter_49165585218_71a2b47049_c.jpg|thumb|Porter dunking over [[Dzanan Musa]] of the [[Brooklyn Nets]]]] Standing at 6 feet 5 inches (1.96 meters) with a 6 ft. 9 in. wingspan (2.05 m), Porter plays both the point guard and shooting guard positions. On offense, he possesses a strong isolation game that is complemented by a high level of athleticism that allows him to be an effective scorer on the perimeter, at and above the rim, and in transition.{{Cite web|title=Kevin Porter|url=https://www.nbadraft.net/players/kevin-porter/|access-date=2021-10-01|website=NBADraft.net|language=en-US|archive-date=October 1, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211001062731/https://www.nbadraft.net/players/kevin-porter/|url-status=live}} His elite handling skills allow him to create space and defer to either a step-back jumper, a pull-up shot out of a crossover, or a behind-the-back dribble pull-back.{{Cite web|last=Joe.hulbert|date=2019-06-04|title=Assessing the Draft's Most Polarizing Prospect: Kevin Porter, Jr.|url=https://www.canishoopus.com/2019/6/4/18650385/assessing-the-drafts-most-polarizing-prospect-kevin-porter-jr-nba-draft|access-date=2021-10-01|website=Canis Hoopus|language=en|archive-date=October 1, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211001062731/https://www.canishoopus.com/2019/6/4/18650385/assessing-the-drafts-most-polarizing-prospect-kevin-porter-jr-nba-draft|url-status=live}}{{Cite web|last=Vecenie|first=Sam|title=Vecenie's NBA Draft Superlatives: 50 names and thoughts about what happened in the draft|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/1039665/2019/06/24/vecenies-nba-draft-superlatives-50-names-and-thoughts-about-what-happened-in-the-draft/|access-date=2021-10-01|website=The Athletic|language=en|archive-date=October 1, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211001062728/https://theathletic.com/1039665/2019/06/24/vecenies-nba-draft-superlatives-50-names-and-thoughts-about-what-happened-in-the-draft/|url-status=live}} Scouts have pointed out his defense and rebounding abilities as another strength, forcing turnovers and running the ball down the court. ==Personal life== ===Weapons charge=== On November 15, 2020, Porter Jr. was charged by [[Mahoning County]] police following a single car accident for improper handling of a firearm in a vehicle. In a statement the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] stated, "We are aware of the situation involving Kevin Porter Jr. and are in the process of gathering information. We have spoken with Kevin and will continue to address this privately with him as the related process evolves."{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/30322395/cleveland-cavaliers-kevin-porter-jr-arrested-weapon-charge|title=Cleveland Cavaliers' Kevin Porter Jr. arrested on weapon charge|work=[[ESPN]]|author=[[Associated Press]]|date=November 15, 2020|access-date=November 15, 2020|archive-date=November 15, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201115183748/https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/30322395/cleveland-cavaliers-kevin-porter-jr-arrested-weapon-charge|url-status=live}} A grand jury in Mahoning County declined to indict Porter on the felony gun charge. It was determined that both the vehicle and the gun belonged to his mother.{{cite news |last1=Feigan |first1=Jonathan |title=Rockets trade Kevin Porter Jr. to Oklahoma City for Victor Oladipo, Jeremiah Robinson-Earl |url=https://www.houstonchronicle.com/texas-sports-nation/rockets/article/houston-rockets-trade-kevin-porter-jr-to-okc-18431134.php |access-date=17 October 2023 |work=Houston Chronicle |date=17 October 2023}} Misdemeanor charges of driving without a license were also dropped.{{cite web|url=https://www.mahoningmatters.com/local-news/mahoning-grand-jury-passes-on-firearm-indictment-for-cavs-kevin-porter-jr-3194087|title=Mahoning grand jury passes on firearm indictment for Cavs' Kevin Porter Jr.|work=Mahoning Matters|first=Justin|last=Dennis|date=December 17, 2020|access-date=January 19, 2021|archive-date=December 17, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201217225653/https://www.mahoningmatters.com/local-news/mahoning-grand-jury-passes-on-firearm-indictment-for-cavs-kevin-porter-jr-3194087|url-status=live}} ===Domestic violence charge=== On September 11, 2023, Porter Jr. was arrested and charged by the [[New York Police Department]] for assaulting his girlfriend, [[Kysre Gondrezick]].{{cite web|first1=Josh|last1=Margolin|first2=Aaron|last2=Katersky|title=Houston Rockets guard Kevin Porter Jr. arrested for domestic violence: Sources|url=https://abcnews.go.com/Sports/houston-rockets-guard-kevin-porter-jr-arrested-domestic/story?id=103091953|work=[[ABC News (United States)|ABC News]]|date=September 11, 2023|access-date=September 11, 2023|archive-date=September 11, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230911170041/https://abcnews.go.com/Sports/houston-rockets-guard-kevin-porter-jr-arrested-domestic/story?id=103091953|url-status=live}} Gondrezick was left with a cut above her eye and a fractured vertabra. Afterwards the [[Houston Rockets]] barred Porter from having any interaction with the team. After the Rockets traded Porter to the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] on October 17, he was immediately waived by the Thunder.{{cite web|first=Kristie|last=Rieken|title=Kevin Porter barred from Houston Rockets after domestic violence arrest in New York|url=https://apnews.com/article/rockets-porter-arrest-domestic-violence-8dc4fd2aedd3c6f46f8c058393f61076|work=[[AP News]]|date=October 2, 2023|access-date=October 2, 2023}} On January 23, 2024, he accepted a deal, pleading guilty to a misdemeanor charge of reckless assault and a second-degree harassment violation.{{cite web | last1=Iko | first1=Kelly | last2=Rosenstein | first2=Greg | title=Former Rockets guard Kevin Porter Jr. reaches plea deal on assault, harassment charges | website=The Athletic | date=2024-01-24 | url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/5222137/2024/01/23/kevin-porter-jr-plea-deal/ | access-date=2025-12-13}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend}} ===NBA=== ====Regular season==== {{NBA player statistics start}} |- | style="text-align:left;"| {{nbay|2019}} | style="text-align:left;"| [[2019–20 Cleveland Cavaliers season|Cleveland]] | 50 || 3 || 23.2 || .442 || .335 || .723 || 3.2 || 2.2 || .9 || .3 || 10.0 |- | style="text-align:left;"| {{nbay|2020}} | style="text-align:left;"| [[2020–21 Houston Rockets season|Houston]] | 26 || 23 || 32.1 || .400 || .368 || .734 || 3.8 || 6.3 || .7 || .3 || 16.6 |- | style="text-align:left;"| {{nbay|2021}} | style="text-align:left;"| [[2021–22 Houston Rockets season|Houston]] | '''61''' || '''61''' || 31.3 || .415 || .375 || .642 || 4.4 || 6.2 || 1.1 || .4 || 15.6 |- | style="text-align:left;"| {{nbay|2022}} | style="text-align:left;"| [[2022–23 Houston Rockets season|Houston]] | 59 || 59 || '''34.3''' || .442 || .366 || .784 || '''5.3''' || 5.7 || 1.4 || .3 || '''19.2''' |- | rowspan=2 style="text-align:left;"| {{nbay|2024}} | style="text-align:left;"| [[2024–25 Los Angeles Clippers season|L.A.
